news.headline: Ravens unsure if QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play Week 5
news.summary: Jackson sprained his ankle scrambling in Week 4 and left the stadium in a boot; Ian Rapoport reports he has only an outside chance to play Sunday against Atlanta, with Tyler Huntley set to start if he sits — a direct hit to Zay Flowers' ceiling either way.

news.headline: Chargers QB Justin Herbert's finger injury not considered major
news.summary: Herbert fractured a finger on his non-throwing hand, played through it with a glove, and isn't considered at risk for Week 5 against Denver.

news.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins (adductor) still day-to-day entering Week 5
news.summary: Higgins remains day-to-day on the adductor strain from Sunday's game at Jacksonville, with no clean official practice tag confirmed yet ahead of Sunday's trip to Miami.

news.headline: Rams QB Matthew Stafford dealing hip injury
news.summary: Stafford is managing a hip contusion from Week 4 but head coach Sean McVay expects him close to full-go for Monday night's game against Buffalo.

news.headline: Eagles lose Dallas Goedert, Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith to injury
news.summary: Philadelphia enters the London game against Jacksonville missing three key offensive weapons, which should make life easier on the Jaguars defense and soften the Eagles' already-middling implied total.

news.headline: Bengals WR Dohnte Meyers climbing the depth chart behind Higgins
news.summary: With Andrei Iosivas on IR, former CFL standout Dohnte Meyers is now the Bengals' clear WR3 behind Chase and Higgins, making him a direct speculative add given Higgins' recurring injury flags.

news.headline: Mike Gesicki profiles as Bengals' lead receiving TE for 2026
news.summary: With Noah Fant having left for New Orleans, Gesicki is the clear top receiving option at tight end in Cincinnati, running a route on the highest snap rate of any NFL TE last year — still a priority waiver add, unclaimed as of this run.

news.headline: Bhayshul Tuten Firmly Establishing Himself as Jaguars' Lead Back
news.summary: Tuten has pulled away as Jacksonville's clear lead back in snaps and touches, with Chris Rodriguez Jr. a complementary piece rather than a real threat to the job.

news.headline: Jaguars' Parker Washington emerging as go-to target
news.summary: With Travis Hunter out for the season (knee surgery) and Brian Thomas Jr. dealing with a high-ankle sprain, Washington has stepped into the lead receiving role — 28 catches, 330 yards, 2 TD over the past three games.

news.headline: Rams backfield could shift toward a 50/50 Corum-Williams split
news.summary: Kyren Williams and Blake Corum remain atop the Rams' RB depth chart with a workload trending toward an even split rather than a clear lead back — caps Corum's ceiling even in good matchups.

news.headline: Browns place RB Dylan Sampson (knee) on injured reserve
news.summary: Sampson, who was earmarked for third-down work behind Quinshon Judkins, landed on IR with a knee injury, pushing Raheim Sanders into the backup role.

news.headline: Bengals Depth Chart Preview: Running back room follows Chase Brown's indisputable lead
news.summary: Perine remains Cincinnati's clear RB2 behind Chase Brown, a non-threatening change-of-pace piece with no standalone value while Brown is healthy.

news.headline: Eagles Place RB Tank Bigsby On IR; Saquon Barkley Likely to Miss Week 5
news.summary: Bigsby underwent core-muscle surgery and landed on injured reserve, with a timeline that could keep him out into November.

season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.

Tyler Shough (22.38, waiver QB stash) outscored started QB Justin Herbert (9.88) by 12.5 — not a real swap given Shough's a Saints starter you don't play, but the bigger miss was starting Michael Wilson (3.8) over bench WR Josh Downs (14.2), a 10.4-point gap; the Week 3 lineup already has that fixed. Also: Zay Flowers stayed rostered through a scoreless Week 2 (ruled Out, no IR move) — a wasted bench spot two weeks running.

Michael Wilson (25.9) outscored started Josh Downs (12.7) by 13.2 on the bench — the second straight week a bench WR beat a starter by double digits. Backup QB Tyler Shough (24.8) also beat Herbert (13.74) again. Tempting as that pattern looks, don't chase last week's points by benching your clearly better asset — that exact overcorrection sat live in your Week 4 lineup for five straight days (Shough over Herbert) until this run flagged it again.

Left the QB slot completely empty all week (Shough would've scored 15.94 sitting there unused) and started Josh Downs (4.6) over Omarion Hampton (13.3) in the flex — an 8.7-point unforced error stacked on a totally wasted roster slot. A win over a weak opponent papered over the worst bench-management week of the season so far; double-check every single slot is filled before Thursday lock, every week, no exceptions.
